judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The element is the teaser photo of the first NEWS card. It is a standalone img, not inside a link, and its alt repeats the headline of the h3 link right below it. The crop and screenshot show a parked police patrol car on a street: no woman, no open door, no chase, so the claim that the alternative describes something the image does not show is true of the capture. My own reading is that it fails 1.1.1: the alternative neither conveys what the photo shows nor lets assistive technology ignore an illustrative photo (alt=""), and it suggests the picture shows the incident. But the headline used as alt for a news teaser photo is a pattern competent auditors split on: many treat the photo as a supplement to the adjacent headline and the alt as merely redundant (a best-practice issue, like axe's image-redundant-alt), not a 1.1.1 failure. So the label is uncertain. The live homepage, fetched on 2026-11-21 shortly after the capture, serves the same teaser markup (same img, alt and surrounding article), and the screenshot shows the same card, so the capture does not differ in a way that matters.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the topic tag link 'Arnold' (aria-label Arnold, href all-about/arnold) in the footer of the 'Delighted punters flood into pub reopened' teaser; the heading just before it is that card's h3. It leads to https://www.nottinghampost.com/all-about/arnold, which I opened: its title is 'Arnold news and views' and its h1 is 'Arnold', a topic page for the Nottinghamshire town. The link text names exactly the subject of the page it opens, and Understanding 2.4.4 does not require the page's full title, so its purpose (go to Arnold news) is determinable from the text alone; the claim that the text does not tell where the link goes is therefore not true. No other link on the page is named Arnold, so R1 does not apply. Rampa never read the destination, which would have shown it is the Arnold topic page. The live page serves the same tag link and the screenshot shows the ARNOLD tag under the headline, so the capture does not differ.
